title: The Gentle Letting Go Saturday
skyStory: The moon begins to shrink, a waning gibbous still in Aries, ninety-three percent lit and starting to wind down after a very busy week. It is taking off its shoes. Mars helps it out of its jacket. The sky smells faintly like a campfire that has been put out properly. Saturn tucks the moon in and leaves the hall light on.

reading: After the big fire of the full moon, today is for sweeping up the ashes. Clear one thing off your plate. Not finish it, clear it: decide you are not doing it, and let it go. The [[Eight of Cups]] walks away from a pile of perfectly fine cups, and it feels great about it.

Saturday at the cabin is for small comforts. A slow morning. A long walk under trees just starting to turn. A nap that nobody judges. The Tiger curls up by the stove and finally lets someone else stoke the fire. If anyone offers to cook, clean or drive, say yes.
joel.mission: Pick one project or commitment that no longer sparks joy, and officially retire it with a short farewell speech.
joel.omen: A pile of leaves blowing apart in the wind. Letting go of something will feel light, not sad.

reading: The Wood Rat has been gathering a lot lately, ideas, plans, little bits of other people's problems. Today, check your stash. Some of it is not yours to carry. Return it gently. You are allowed to help people without holding their whole basket.

In the afternoon, a pocket of quiet will open, maybe twenty minutes, maybe an hour. Do not fill it. Sit in it. Let your hands rest in your lap instead of telling a story. Your Life Path 11 does its best work in silence, and today it is cooking up something lovely for next week.
nancy.mission: Give one problem back to the person it belongs to, kindly, with a clear and gentle sentence.
nancy.omen: A bird dropping a twig and flying off lighter. You can set something down today.

together.text: Each of you write down one worry on a scrap of paper, then tear it into tiny pieces and send a photo of the confetti. Declare it gone. The waning moon will haul the confetti off to the far side of the sky.
